title: Round 131 (F437): Monster shadow/light system - 0x40B180 caller (mode [0x61BD4]: 0=dim (5,5,10), 2=bright (100,100,100), 8=flash (255,255,255), else (10,255,255,255)) -> 0x434A20 hex-grid radial light renderer (fsqrt distance falloff, RGB32 blend, 6-vertex quad-fan, 0x12/0x11 hex pitch) on global 0x7DA1D8; 0x434670 = pixel->hex-cell (x+8)*2/3, y>>5
objective: Decode the monster shadow/light effect render path: caller, renderer, and coordinate conversion.
question: How does the client draw monster shadows and hit-flashes?

renderer_0x434A20.grid: hex cells (0x12=18px pitch, 0x11=17 row offset, 0x6C0 base, 0x30=48 row stride)
renderer_0x434A20.write: 6-vertex quad-fan (5 words) per cell into 32-bit RGB buffer

exe_trace.hex_grid: isometric light grid (not pixel buffer) - 0x12/0x11/0x6C0 constants

audit_vs_exe.F435: draw path: shadow call site 0x40B1BC confirmed in anim machine
audit_vs_exe.F375: separate from map blit (0x43B440) - light system independent

contrast.light_vs_tiles: hex-cell light field vs 32px square tile buffer (F379)
contrast.dim_vs_flash: shadow dim (5,5,10) vs hit flash (255,255,255) = same renderer, different color args

verdict: Monster shadow/light system PRIMARY-verified: 0x40B180 caller with mode [0x61BD4] (dim/bright/flash), 0x434A20 hex-grid radial renderer (fsqrt distance, RGB32 blend, quad-fan), 0x434670 pixel->hex conversion, global 0x7DA1D8.
notes: hex cell stride 0x30 row / 0x12 col = isometric packing
radius gate 0x7E1 caps light field extent
